##Table 2
library(ordinal)

#harm perceptions of e-cigarettes - main effects model
model1 <- ordinal::clmm(
  harm_score_factor ~  Condition + Sex + Ethnicity + Age  + white + asian + black + multi + other + sm_freq_use + infl_expos + sub_30dayuse + harm_pretest_binary + (1 | ResponseId),
  data = data_harm,
  link = "logit",
  Hess = TRUE,
 control = ordinal::clmm.control(
    method  = "nlminb",
    maxIter = 5000
  )
)
summary(model1)

##produce adjusted odds ratios, p-values and adjusted p-values, use for all the models
library(broom.mixed)
t1 = tidy(model1,conf.int=TRUE,exponentiate=TRUE,effects="fixed")

p <- t1$p.value
t1$adjust.pvalue <- p.adjust(p, method = "BH")
t1$adjust.pvalue = round(t1$adjust.pvalue,3)
t1$p.value = round(t1$p.value,3)
print(t1, n=50)

#ASSESS COMPLETE VERSUS MISSING CASSES 
library(dplyr)

# select variables from datasets in long format for each outcome: harm perceptoins, appeal and susceptibility
model_vars <- c("harm_score_factor","Condition","Sex","Ethnicity","Age",
                "white","asian","black","multi","other",
                "sm_freq_use","infl_expos","sub_30dayuse","harm_pretest_binary")

model_vars <- c("vape_appeal_t3","Condition","Sex","Ethnicity","Age",
                "white","asian","black","multi","other",
                "sm_freq_use","infl_expos","sub_30dayuse","vape_appeal_pretest_sum")

model_vars <- c("suscept_total","Condition","Sex","Ethnicity","Age",
                "white","asian","black","multi","other",
                "sm_freq_use","infl_expos","cigcan_30dayuse","suscept_pretest")


# 1) Per-ID: how many COMPLETE rows (i.e., rows with NO NA in any model var)
miss_by_id <- data_harm  %>%
  mutate(row_complete = if_all(all_of(model_vars), ~ !is.na(.))) %>%
  group_by(ResponseId) %>%
  summarise(
    n_rows = n(),
    n_complete_rows = sum(row_complete),
    any_missing = n_complete_rows < n_rows,          # has at least one incomplete row
    included_in_clmm = n_complete_rows > 0,          # contributes ≥1 row to CLMM
    missing_group = if_else(included_in_clmm, "complete", "missing"),  # 674 vs 26
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# 2) One row per participant for baseline covariates (no outcome needed here)
library(dplyr)
baseline_covars <- data_harm %>%
  select(ResponseId, harm_score_factor, Condition, Sex, Ethnicity, Age, white, asian, black, multi, other,
         sm_freq_use, infl_expos, sub_30dayuse, harm_pretest_binary, credibility_median_rescale) %>%
  distinct(ResponseId, .keep_all = TRUE)

baseline_covars <- data_appeal %>%
  select(ResponseId, vape_appeal_t3, Condition, Sex, Ethnicity, Age, white, asian, black, multi, other,
         sm_freq_use, infl_expos, sub_30dayuse, vape_appeal_pretest_sum, credibility_median_rescale) %>%
  distinct(ResponseId, .keep_all = TRUE)

baseline_covars <- data_susceptibilty %>%
  select(ResponseId, suscept_total, Condition, Sex, Ethnicity, Age, white, asian, black, multi, other,
         sm_freq_use, infl_expos, cigcan_30dayuse, suscept_pretest, credibility_median_rescale) %>%
  distinct(ResponseId, .keep_all = TRUE)

# 3) Join + counts
comp_id <- baseline_covars %>%
  left_join(miss_by_id, by = "ResponseId")

table(comp_id$missing_group)        # should give "complete" (included) and "missing" (excluded) - a var indicated complete or missing status
table(comp_id$included_in_clmm)     # TRUE/FALSE version


# Examples: Sex, Ethnicity: chi-square
chisq.test(table(comp_id$missing_group, comp_id$Sex))
chisq.test(table(comp_id$missing_group, comp_id$Ethnicity))


#Supplementary table 6
library(mice)

###harm perception
vars <- c("ResponseId","harm_score_factor","Condition","Sex","Ethnicity","Age",
          "white","asian","black","multi","other",
          "sm_freq_use","infl_expos","sub_30dayuse","harm_pretest_binary",
          "credibility_median_rescale")  # optional but OK to include

dat <- data_harm[, vars]

# ---- methods ----
meth <- make.method(dat)

meth["ResponseId"]       <- ""   # don't impute ID
meth["Condition"]       <- ""   # randomized; do not impute
meth["harm_score_factor"]<- ""   # outcome; do not impute (leave missing as-is)

# Only these have missingness:
meth["Sex"]                 <- "logreg"    # if binary; else use "polyreg"
meth["Ethnicity"]           <- "logreg"    # if binary; else use "polyreg"
meth["sm_freq_use"]         <- "polyreg"   # 3+ categories (unordered)
meth["harm_pretest_binary"] <- "logreg"    # binary

# credibility is continuous -> PMM is appropriate
meth["credibility_median_rescale"] <- "pmm"

# ---- predictor matrix ----
pred <- make.predictorMatrix(dat)

# don't use / predict IDs
pred[, "ResponseId"] <- 0
pred["ResponseId", ] <- 0

# don't let the outcome be used to impute covariates (avoids outcome-informed imputation)
pred[, "harm_score_factor"] <- 0

# also don't impute the outcome (already meth["harm_score_factor"] <- "")
pred["harm_score_factor", ] <- 0


# ---- run imputation ---- main effect harm
imp <- mice(dat,
            m = 20, maxit = 50, seed = 500,
            method = meth, predictorMatrix = pred)

# quick check
imp


# ---- run imputation ---- interaction effect harm
imp2 <- mice(dat,
            m = 20, maxit = 50, seed = 501,
            method = meth, predictorMatrix = pred)

# quick check
imp2

data_list <- complete(imp, "all")

##main effect
fits <- lapply(data_list, function(d){
  clmm(harm_score_factor ~ Condition + Sex + Ethnicity + Age +
         white + asian + black + multi + other +
         sm_freq_use + infl_expos + sub_30dayuse + harm_pretest_binary +
         (1|ResponseId),
       data=d, link="logit", Hess=TRUE,
       control=clmm.control(method="nlminb", maxIter=5000))
})#2 removed, mean_sd median_sd   sd_of_sd   min_sd   max_sd
            # 3.332918  3.339762 0.02307806 3.247852 3.355417

##interaction effect
fits2 <- lapply(data_list, function(d){
  clmm(harm_score_factor ~ Condition*credibility_median_rescale + Sex + Ethnicity + Age +
         white + asian + black + multi + other +
         sm_freq_use + infl_expos + sub_30dayuse + harm_pretest_binary +
         (1|ResponseId),
       data=d, link="logit", Hess=TRUE,
       control=clmm.control(method="nlminb", maxIter=5000))
})


# Extract only Condition rows from each fit
extract_cond <- function(m){
  s <- summary(m)
  tab <- as.data.frame(s$coefficients)
  tab$term <- rownames(tab)
  tab <- tab[grepl("credibility", tab$term), c("term","Estimate","Std. Error")]
  rownames(tab) <- NULL
  tab
}

est_list <- lapply(fits, extract_cond)#replaced with fits2 for interaction effects

# Note: ordinal mixed models (CLMMs) adjusted for the corresponding baseline outcome may be unstable
# in some imputed datasets because the baseline harm/appeal perception measure is highly predictive
# of the post-exposure ordinal outcome. This can produce large SEs or
# non-convergence. Non-converged or unstable models are excluded from pooled
# sensitivity estimates. This reflects estimation instability from a highly predictive
# covariate, not inconsistency in the substantive findings.

# mark "good" fits: all Condition SEs are present and finite
is_good <- sapply(est_list, function(x){
  all(is.finite(x$Estimate)) && all(is.finite(x$`Std. Error`))
})

# additionally drop these imputations for a sensitivity test

which(!is_good)   # show which produced non-invertible Hessians (no valid SEs)
fits_use     <- fits[is_good]
est_list_use <- est_list[is_good]
m_use <- length(fits_use)
message("Pooling uses m = ", m_use, " imputations (dropped: ", paste(which(!is_good), collapse=", "), ").")

is_good <- sapply(est_list, function(x){
  all(is.finite(x$Estimate)) && all(is.finite(x$`Std. Error`))
})


# --- 2) pool across the remaining imputations (NA-robust) ---
terms <- sort(Reduce(union, lapply(est_list_use, `[[`, "term")))

B  <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = m_use, ncol = length(terms),
             dimnames = list(paste0("imp", seq_len(m_use)), terms))
SE <- B

for(i in seq_along(est_list_use)){
  xi <- est_list_use[[i]]
  B[i,  xi$term] <- xi$Estimate
  SE[i, xi$term] <- xi$`Std. Error`
}

m_eff <- colSums(!is.na(B) & !is.na(SE))

bbar <- colMeans(B, na.rm = TRUE)
W    <- colMeans(SE^2, na.rm = TRUE)
Bm   <- apply(B, 2, stats::var, na.rm = TRUE)

Tvar <- W + (1 + 1/m_use) * Bm
se_p <- sqrt(Tvar)

OR   <- exp(bbar)
CI_L <- exp(bbar - 1.96*se_p)
CI_U <- exp(bbar + 1.96*se_p)

pooled_test <- data.frame(
  term = names(bbar),
  logOR = bbar,
  SE = se_p,
  OR = OR,
  CI_L = CI_L,
  CI_U = CI_U,
  m_eff = m_eff,
  m_used = m_use,
  row.names = NULL
)



# --- add p-values + BH correction to your pooled table ---
# (run after you create `pooled`)
pooled_test$z <- pooled_test$logOR / pooled_test$SE
pooled_test$p <- 2 * pnorm(abs(pooled_test$z), lower.tail = FALSE)   # two-sided Wald p
pooled_test$p_BH <- p.adjust(pooled_test$p, method = "BH")
